blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — postoperative pulmonary-complication prevention
stem: A postoperative client is at risk for atelectasis after abdominal surgery. Which nursing plan best supports postoperative lung expansion?

options.A: Encourage deep breathing and directed coughing, promote early mobility, provide adequate analgesia, and use incentive spirometry as an adjunct rather than as the sole strategy.
options.B: Rely on incentive spirometry as the primary preventive measure while delaying ambulation and coughing until the client can use the device without discomfort.
options.C: Maintain bed rest and limit coughing to protect the incision, adding supplemental oxygen if dyspnea develops instead of using routine lung-expansion measures.
options.D: Minimize position changes and mobility to reduce incisional discomfort because postoperative movement and directed coughing increase the risk of atelectasis.

rationale: The AARC incentive-spirometry guideline states that incentive spirometry alone is not recommended for routine prevention of postoperative pulmonary complications and recommends combining it with deep-breathing techniques, directed coughing, early mobilization, and optimal analgesia. AARC airway-clearance guidance also supports early mobility/ambulation in postoperative patients. Therefore A is correct.
educational_objective: Use multimodal postoperative lung-expansion measures—deep breathing, directed coughing, early mobility, and adequate analgesia—with incentive spirometry as an adjunct rather than a stand-alone intervention.
source_document_title: AARC Clinical Practice Guideline: Incentive Spirometry; Effectiveness of Nonpharmacologic Airway Clearance Therapies in Hospitalized Patients
source_version_date: AARC CPGs published 2011 and 2013 and remain available as AARC guideline resources; accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: Incentive Spirometry recommendations 14.1-14.3: IS alone not recommended; use with deep breathing, directed coughing, early mobilization, and optimal analgesia. Airway-clearance CPG postoperative recommendations: early mobility/ambulation recommended; routine prophylactic IS not recommended.
source_claim_supported: Postoperative pulmonary prevention is multimodal; incentive spirometry should not be relied upon as a stand-alone routine strategy, and early mobility is recommended.
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential: use precautions to prevent complications associated with procedures/diagnoses and provide postoperative education.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Removed only-based cueing and rewrote all choices as complete postoperative prevention plans.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches AARC postoperative pulmonary-prevention guidance; no residual absolute-word cue or second answer remains.
